contradictions.statement: The actual r19 C3 receipt and its tool emit no evidence markers. Under the contract (missing marker = invalid), a faithful r19 snapshot can only yield code 2 evidence_audit_input_invalid. The registration requires both 'red on a faithful actual r19 C3 receipt represented without changing rows' and 'green only when scoped to five observed plus one lead'. Neither is reachable without adding evidence keys to all 11 rows, which is a row change.

Unit of count mismatch. 'observed5/6 plus lead1/6' is the incident-line split (tw-recall-split totals). The contract counts finding rows. The faithful population is 11 rows = 10 observed + 1 lead. The SCORECARD's literal 'correct scope' claim {total 6, observed 5, lead 1} evaluated against the faithful 11-row snapshot is RED (finding_count_mismatch, observed_count_mismatch). The only green claim in contract units is {total 11, observed 10, lead 1, errors 0, clean false}. Collapsing to 6 one-per-line rows deletes 5 real findings, i.e. changes rows.
evidence: audit-contract.json rules 'Claim total, observed, lead and errors each equal the actual corresponding count'

contradictions.statement: r19 never asserted 'observed 6/6'. It asserted detected 6, score 10.0, with any-class/any-evidence detection. The 'observed6/6' red assertion is a reconstruction. In contract row units it is {total 11, observed 11, lead 0, errors 0, clean false}. This must be labeled as a translation of a 'detected' claim, not a quoted r19 claim.
evidence: tw-recall.py docstring: 'at least one finding (any class, unpermitted or not)'

It is the same detector lineage C1 modifies. No committed split exists for 46c82902, which is the current C1 base at 741122d. Whether the base or the candidate labels that row lead is UNKNOWN (not measured, by contract). Source authority independently supports 'lead': the round-18 note says the query runs through local helper run_record, and its definition (line 437) is outside the pinned bytes, so execution is not observable from the frozen snapshot.

coupling_routes.statement: The r20 split has no files counters and no command strings. If HistoricalC3 or AuditHarness fills the evidence, command or files fields by re-scanning frozen inputs with HEAD or candidate tools/mado-tripwire.py, the C2 historical outcome becomes a function of C1 bytes. Any intervention that swaps classifier bytes after the fixture is frozen cannot detect this, because the fixture already carries C1's output.
coupling_routes.status: open until the historical snapshot's provenance is pinned to pre-base blobs

coupling_routes.statement: The r21-style runner stages only the gate, the classifier and the fixtures. A dependency on any other lane path (.ufo/waves/round-22/oracle/*, other tools/*, git objects) sees that path absent in all three states, so output equality holds vacuously.

Output equality tests whether verdicts depend on C1. The registered clause is stronger: C2 'never imports/runs C1, reads its source'. A gate that executes or reads C1 and discards the result passes equality.

Nothing shows the intervention harness can detect a coupled gate. Equality without a sensitivity control is unfalsifiable; a harness that copied the same bytes for every state would also report equality.
r21 ran only --selftest. The r22 historical target is a --check BUNDLE --root ROOT verdict. An intervention that omits the exact admission argv does not cover the admitted claim.

AuditHarness is told to reuse the round21 capped runner, as OracleHarness is. If audit/measure.py imports or reads oracle/ code, C2 measurement depends on C1 harness bytes. Separately, if Main credits C1 disclosure using C2 --check on C1 receipts, C1 admission depends on C2 (C2 -> C1).

The contract sums only eval_unparsed and unparsed_spawns, and it does not reject unknown file keys. If C1 records unknown-capture uncertainty in a new counter or evidence value, C2 would undercount errors on C1-era receipts and call an error-bearing scan clean. This does not affect frozen fixtures, but it bounds what C2's capability claim may say about future receipts.

channel_B_runtime_intervention.tree: Full-tree extraction of the candidate commit via `git archive <commit> | tar -x -C $TMP` (no worktree; no Git index or jj mutation). Vary only the C1 surfaces.
states: read-detector: path replaced by a named FIFO; any open() blocks until the 15 s cap, so a read becomes a timeout divergence
exec-detector: path replaced by inert bytes that only create a marker file inside $TMP when executed; marker presence is a violation even when stdout is equal
harness-hostile: .ufo/waves/round-22/oracle/ replaced by the same FIFO/marker pair (covers R2/R6)
channel_B_runtime_intervention.argv_per_state: The exact admission argv: `python3 -I tools/mado-evidence-audit.py --selftest FIXTURE_ROOT` plus `--check BUNDLE --root ROOT` for every audit bundle, including all four historical variants. One child at a time, 384 MiB, 15 s.
channel_B_runtime_intervention.equality: Byte equality of (exit, stdout, stderr) for each argv across base, changed and absent. No timeout in read-detector. No marker in exec-detector or harness-hostile. Fixture-tree sha256 unchanged before and after every state.
channel_B_runtime_intervention.positive_control: A staged, harness-local copy of the gate with one appended line that hashes tools/mado-tripwire.py into stdout. It must produce UNEQUAL base/changed output and a read-detector timeout. Never written to tools/; discarded after the receipt. Without this, equality is not evidence (R4).
channel_B_runtime_intervention.reverse_direction: The C1 oracle verdict bytes (OracleHarness measure output and expected.sha256) must be equal with tools/mado-evidence-audit.py present, absent and FIFO. C1 admission MUST NOT consume any C2 --check verdict.

proposed_move.disclosure_for_R7: C2's capability statement is limited to receipts whose uncertainty lives entirely in eval_unparsed and unparsed_spawns. If C1 adds any other uncertainty counter or evidence value, Main records that C2 does not cover it. No contract change is proposed.

risks: Channel A uses labels emitted by detectors from rejected rounds (9613f510 and a57d4fe9). Using them as frozen data admits nothing. Its validity rests on the source grounding (K4); if HistoricalC3 finds a source disagreement on any of the 11 rows, the joined variant must be dropped, not relabeled.

Even when grounded, the joined variant is a translated artifact, not the 'faithful actual r19 receipt'. The registration wording (K1) cannot be met literally; Main must choose and disclose. This proposal does not shrink scope silently.
The read-detector FIFO costs up to 15 s per argv when C2 misbehaves. Sequential execution keeps it inside the one-child cap.

Exec-detector bytes must be inert: they only touch a file in $TMP, with no network, host or package action. If Sentinel seats object, drop that state and disclose R3 as unverified rather than weakening the others.
git archive omits untracked w1 artifacts. The candidate commit must contain the sealed fixtures, or they are copied in and their digests recorded.
verification_for_main: Recompute the Channel A snapshot from blobs 10f5a706 and 34bb3ee3 at 741122d. Assert an 11-row 1:1 join and record the snapshot sha256 before any C1 tool commit.
Run the Channel B states and argv after seal. Assert equality and no timeout or marker; assert the positive control diverges.
Reverse check: C1 oracle verdict bytes are invariant to the C2 tool's presence.
Confirm that audit/measure.py has no import or path reference into round-22/oracle/ or tools/mado-tripwire.py (static grep).
